title: [2.1] Build fixes for modern toolchains
body:
The `2.1` branch is no longer maintained, but it's still relevant to keep it buildable if we can, for game preservation, or some use cases like support for older platforms like OUYA or homebrew consoles.

I don't intend to spend a lot of effort on this, but if I can make sure the code is still compatible with recent Python 3, SCons 4, and modern compilers, that's worth a try.

- Android: Fix compatibility with Python 3.13 which removed `distutils`. Not tested, maybe you can check it @bherdm since you need it for OUYA?
- OSX (by @bherdm): Fix compatibility with Xcode 16 (possibly earlier versions, I haven't checked details on when that error started).
  * Fixes #101035.
- C++ standards: Set explicitly the standards we used to target implicitly with GCC 5 back then, i.e. C++98 and C11. For MSVC we can't set anything earlier than C++14 - old VS 2015 and 2017 we used back then should default to something old enough (C++11?). Not sure about VS 2019 and later, and if those are supported at all currently.
- Linux/Windows GCC 6/7 compat: GCC > 5 used to be blocked due to #4623 and related bugs, which were fixed in 3.0 by changing `Object::cast_to` to a static method. From testing various versions, I found that GCC 6/7 do reproduce the bug in `target=release tools=no` (release templates), but not GCC 8, GCC 9, or GCC 14. So presumably whatever optimization caused the crash in GCC 6/7 has been fixed. This is still not Safe™, but It Works™, maybe? I don't really want to spend more time on this nor change the behavior of the codebase. @hpvb has some ideas on how to trick GCC into not doing the problematic optimization though.
- speex: GCC 14 was rightfully complaining about that one. The code seems a bit buggy, and it's still the same in latest upstream but speex is a dead project. I chose to just enforce what would happen implicitly before.
- SCons: Fix some Python scripts missing `close()` on file writes, which broke `AndroidManifest.xml` generation with Python 3.13.1 for me.
- libmpcdec: Fix build issue for templates with MSVC due to overriding `log2` with a macro.
- Web: Fix HTML5 gamepad handling on modern browsers (backports #21588 and #25149).

---

Toolchains tested per target, for release templates (prior to blocking GCC 6/7 again, so I could test them). Tested with the `gui/drag_and_drop` official demo from the `2.1` branch, just running it would crash with a `-O3` optimized release template built with GCC 6.

- Linux
  * Fedora 43, Python 3.14.0, SCons 4.10.0: Both GCC 15.2.1 and Clang 21.1.5
  * Fedora 41, Python 3.13.1, SCons 4.8.1: Both GCC 14.2.1 and Clang 19.1.5
  * Ubuntu 16.04, Python 2.7.12, SCons 2.4.1: GCC 6.5.0 (crash), 7.5.0 (crash), 8.4.0 (works), 9.4.0 (works)
  * Ubuntu 16.10, Python 2.7.12, SCons 2.5.0: GCC 6.2.0 and 6.1.1 (installed manually) (both crash)
- Server
  * Ubuntu 16.04, Python 2.7.12, SCons 2.4.1: GCC 6.5.0 (works - not using `-O3`)
- Windows
  * Ubuntu 16.04, Python 2.7.12, SCons 2.4.1: MinGW GCC 5.4.0 (works)
  * Ubuntu 16.10, Python 2.7.12, SCons 2.5.0: MinGW GCC 6.2.0 (crash)
- macOS
  * macOS 15.2, Xcode 16.2: Works fine (tested by @bruvzg in https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/101040#pullrequestreview-2528659198)
  * Fedora 41, Python 3.13.0, SCons 4.8.1: osxcross with Xcode 16.2 SDK, Apple Clang 17.0.6 (both editor and release templates build fine with explicit `osxcross_sdk=darwin24.2`, didn't test binaries)
- Android
  * Fedora 41, Python 3.13.1, SCons 4.8.1: NDK r17c 17.2.4988734, Temurin JDK 8 (builds fine, didn't test apk)
- iOS
  * Fedora 41, Python 3.13.0, SCons 4.8.1: osxcross with Xcode 16.2 SDK, Apple Clang 17.0.6 (builds fine with explicit `IPHONESDK="/root/ioscross/arm64/SDK/iPhoneOS18.2.sdk/" IPHONEPATH="/root/ioscross/arm64/" SDKVERSION=18.2 ios_triple="arm-apple-darwin11-"`, didn't test binaries)
- Web
  * Fedora 41, Python 3.13.1, SCons 4.8.1: Emscripten 1.38.34 to Emscripten 1.39.1-fastcomp tested, builds successfully, doesn't run in modern browsers anymore
- BB10, Haiku, WinRT: Out of scope, not supported
